findings.issue: A wrong OTP calls recordFailure even while the account is already locked. Each one bumps failed_attempts and resets locked_until to now plus up to 15m. The password path works differently: AuthUserDetails rejects a locked account before the hash check, so nothing is recorded during a lock. Through OTP, an attacker who knows only the phone can keep the lock extended with no gap. verifyCode returns false even when no code was issued, so no SMS is needed and the OTP caps do not apply. That contradicts the doc and edge-case claim 'never permanent' more strongly than the password path does.
findings.fix: Inside the wrong-code branch, call recordFailure only when !loginAttempts.isLocked(user.getId()), and still throw AUTH_OTP_INVALID. This matches password-path semantics and adds no oracle. Otherwise, reword the docs to say a sustained attack can keep the lock in force.

findings.issue: The caps count requests, not sends. A request suppressed by the 30 s resend cooldown still uses up the window and daily caps. A user who taps 'send code' 3 times in a few seconds gets 1 SMS and is then capped for 15 minutes. Counting requests is needed so unknown numbers look the same, and it matches AC-4's wording. But env-descriptions.json and environment-variables.md call AUTH_OTP_PER_PHONE_* 'OTP sends per phone', which is wrong.
findings.fix: Change the docs and env text to 'OTP requests per phone'. Consider noting the cooldown interaction in auth-service.md.

findings.issue: The fallback map is shared by the per-IP counters and the OTP cap counters, and it is cleared all at once at max-tracked-clients. During a Redis outage, a source-address flood on the IP limiter also wipes every phone's OTP cap. Stale window-index keys also stay in the map until a clear.
findings.fix: Accept this and document it (soft control while degraded), or keep a separate bounded map per key prefix. No change needed for this PR if it is documented.

findings.issue: Comments still describe 'the Bucket4j per-IP throttle is per-instance' (also LoginAttemptService.java:27). In environment-variables.md and env-descriptions, AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_REFRESH_CAPACITY still says '(in-memory, per instance)'. These are stale after this change.
findings.fix: Update the Javadoc to 'the per-IP throttle (Redis-shared, fail-open per instance)'. Change the refresh-capacity description to match the login one. Leave the V1 migration comment alone.

findings.issue: The timeout test builds its own 250 ms Lettuce client. It does not exercise the spring.data.redis.timeout and connect-timeout values in application.yml, and its bound (elapsed < 5 s) is loose. Removing the YAML timeout would not fail any test. AC-2's 'not 5xx' is also asserted only at counter level ('never throws'), not through RateLimitFilter.
findings.fix: Optionally tighten the bound to about 1 s, and add a context test asserting RedisProperties.getTimeout() == 250ms.

summary: The change is correct and minimal. SharedWindowCounter runs INCR and a conditional PEXPIRE in one Lua EVAL, which is atomic, so every key gets a TTL and the concurrency test proves 50 unique counts with no overshoot. Keys are auth:rl:{path}:{ip}:{idx}, auth:otp:phone:{E164}:{idx} and auth:otp:day:{E164}:{idx}, with TTL window+30s. Any RuntimeException (closed port, WRONGTYPE script error, 250 ms command timeout) falls back to a bounded per-instance map with a throttled WARN and a 5 s skip, which meets CTO condition 4. RateLimitFilter only swaps the bucket for counter.increment keyed on deviceContexts.clientIp(request). The IP logic is untouched, and the 429 path still goes through ProblemResponseWriter, pinned by a test as status 429, AUTH_RATE_LIMITED, no Retry-After and only Content-Type. The OTP caps run before the user lookup, use PhoneNumbers.normalise output, and are disabled at 0 by the '> 0' guards; OtpCapsDisabledIT proves 12 sends and no keys (CTO 5). OTP verify returns early for unknown or unverified phones without recording anything. Known users go to recordFailure(UUID), which is a no-op without a user_credentials row. LOCKED is reachable only after a correct code, so there is no AC-7 oracle and AC-9 holds; OtpLockoutIT covers OTP-only users, including a successful login afterwards (CTO 2). bucket4j has no remaining code usages, only historical docs (CTO 3). There were no prior 429 tests, and the new IT pins the contract. The SecurityConfig edit is necessary because the filter is built in a @Bean method. The tests would fail if any of these were removed: recordFailure, isLocked, recordSuccess, the cap checks or the Redis key. The main residual issue is minor: wrong OTPs during an active lock keep extending it, which the password path does not do. The other findings are doc wording and stale comments. Register edits are deferred per the run rule.
